root_cause.text: The PASID entry teardown zeroed the entire entry while the Present bit was still set, violating the VT-d specification's ownership handshake and allowing hardware to see an inconsistent state via a torn read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that the current implementation zeros the entire 64-byte entry immediately "while it is active (P=1)" and warns that "hardware could observe an inconsistent state, leading to unpredictable behavior or spurious faults." The patch implements a proper sequence: clear Present bit first, then issue invalidations, and only then zero the remaining fields.

candidates.rationale: This call zeroes the entire PASID entry while the Present bit is still set, violating the VT-d specification's ownership handshake and allowing hardware to see an inconsistent state via a torn read.
Reads the domain ID from the PASID table entry (pte) before clearing; if the entry is torn during hardware read, this value could be inconsistent.
Reads the page table type from the PASID entry before clearing; similarly exposed to torn reads due to the subsequent zeroing of the entry with the Present bit set.
Issues an IOTLB flush after the entry has already been zeroed; proper ordering requires clearing the Present bit first, then flushing, then zeroing the rest to prevent stale hardware translations.
Performs device TLB invalidation after the entry has been zeroed; same ordering problem as the IOTLB flush, contributing to the window where hardware sees inconsistent state.

Drains pending Page Request Queue entries after the teardown; while not directly causing the torn read, it is part of the incorrect teardown sequence where zeroing occurs before proper ownership handshake.
